source_verification_receipts.locator: Official proceedings abstract and bibliographic record
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies K-margin causal partial identification through MOT, proves a plug-in convergence rate, and states minimax optimality for arbitrary K when d≤4.
The paper establishes quadratic n^-2/d plug-in behavior for smooth two-margin OT costs and all-estimator lower-bound theory, rather than an arbitrary-margin MOT frontier.

source_verification_receipts.version: Annales de l'Institut Henri Poincare, Probabilites et Statistiques 60(2), 2024, pp. 824-846
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper is a two-margin empirical-OT lower-complexity-adaptation result, with smooth-cost rate improvements; it is not a K-tuple MOT capacity result.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Official proceedings record; Proposition 3.6 and Theorem 4.3 text corroborated in the conference PDF rendering
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies a covariate-aware binary conditional-transport relaxation, interpolates unconditional and conditional bounds, and gives a finite-sample quadratic-cost result under regular Brenier-potential assumptions.
The preprint provides model-agnostic uniformly valid partial-identification inference based on OT duality; it does not state an arbitrary-K minimax expected-excess-length converse.
